<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `77670858e8aff44fe7da5e2a5bc89cce3e2b847a` — the merge of head `3b5318a22a8ca7614fcf4471689f14bf2acac744` into base `d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 77670858e8aff44fe7da5e2a5bc89cce3e2b847a && git checkout 77670858e8aff44fe7da5e2a5bc89cce3e2b847a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec 3b5318a22a8ca7614fcf4471689f14bf2acac744 && git checkout -B drift-repro d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec && git merge --no-ff 3b5318a22a8ca7614fcf4471689f14bf2acac744

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · `domain:server` seat 2 · `os-project-manager` · `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo` · 2026-10-27T05:31Z · head `3b5318a22a` · #25521 cut 15

The maintainer's standing authorisation for landing reviewed PRs, verbatim: 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」.

1. **Shape:** a draft against `main`. The body opens with `Part of #25521` (not `Fixes`). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial. `skip-changeset` applies because this is a move. `check-governed-merges --pr 26490` reads NOT governed, 1,172 changed lines. None of the four contract faces is touched, so no at-tier review is owed. This is the last cut before the pause (「拆分线已经做了一半的继续完成，然后暂停，等新版本发布后继续」, 2026-10-27T04:17Z); it was in progress when that line was written.
2. **Premise:** the claim `6432488188` asked for a seam table re-measured after cut 14, and it is in the body. The backend fault classifier the order priced at about −216 lands as the whole read-exit fault family at −445 (19,794 → 19,349). The six bodies move into `sql-driver-read-exit-fault.ts` behind `ReadExitFaultHost`, together with the four module-level declarations only they read:
   - `backendStatementFault`
   - `aggregateBackendFault`
   - `distinctBackendFault`
   - the filter, aggregate and distinct unresolvable-column refusals
3. **Move check (the seat's own):** every line removed from `sql-driver.ts` was compared with the new module after stripping indentation. All 490 non-blank lines are present there except five:
   - Two import names (`declareTargetedTable`, `isMissingTableError`) that only the moved bodies read. The module imports them itself.
   - Three declarations that staying code still reads, each gaining `export` in place: `PRE_DDL_QUESTION_SCOPE`, `unsupportedFilterError` and `isFilterNode`.

   `unresolvableColumnNameOf` was already exported from `sql-driver.ts`, and it moves to the module. Its only importer outside the module is a test, which is migrated (see 4). `index.ts` re-exports `sql-driver.js` by name only and names none of these declarations, so the published surface does not move. The dev reports the `.d.ts` hash `0f33bf3f` unchanged, with a positive control.
4. **Path readers, migrated in the same PR:**
   - `sql-driver-compile-refusal-seam.test.ts`'s `INVALID_FILTER` builder scan now reads the third file too, so the moved builder stays enumerated.
   - `sql-driver-unresolvable-where-column-refusal.test.ts` imports `unresolvableColumnNameOf` from its new home.
5. **Readings at base and head (the dev's):** `check:adr-anchors` 1,876 = 1,876; the driver-sql, turso and wasm suites match test for test (4,060 / 2,526 / 746); the AST proof is OK with a negative control.
6. **Gates:** at this stamp every check-run on the head reads success or skipped (path-filtered UI, docs build, dogfood matrix placeholder, opt-in harnesses, skipped changeset check). None reads failed or in progress, and Test Core 1–8, Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are green. Locally the dev reports 53 of 54 derived gates green and `test:repo` green. `dual-build-cjs-loads` was not measured locally and is left to CI's full build.
7. **Out of scope (none filed):**
   - `check:tenant-chokepoint`'s `SCAN_FILES` does not list the new module. The moved bodies hold 0 of the 4 tenant predicates and build no query, and widening the list would be a gate change.
   - `OWN_STATEMENT_FAULT` has no in-file reader left but stays, because `sql-driver-raw-execution.ts` imports it.
   - Three staying docblocks in `sql-driver.ts` still `{@link unresolvableColumnNameOf}`, which now lives in the module. This is comment-only and can go with the restart.
   - The next slice after the pause is the rotation sub-banner (about −118).
8. **Landing:** this seat runs `pr_ready` and then `automerge_enable` through the relay, confirms MERGED on both readings, and records the landing on #25521. The same act moves the card to `pm:on-hold` with a `Restart-when:` naming the next release.
